title: Reservation cadence and flex-scale operational playbook
creator: Avery Chen
summary: Define a repeatable quarterly cadence for capacity reservations and introduce a flexible autoscaling layer (flex-scale) that lets us hedge commitments while meeting latency SLOs for Dedicated customers.
description:
Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity ask for predictable throughput and cost but also need headroom for spikes. Current quarterly planning mixes hard reservations with manual bursts; this creates mismatch between commit cycles and real traffic patterns.

Goal: Produce a playbook and deliverables to operationalize a reservation cadence (calendar, approval gates, renewal windows) and a flex-scale autoscaling capability that automatically uses pooled spare capacity or short-term burst credits to smooth demand while preserving per-route SLOs. The playbook will include product requirements, rollout plan, OKRs, pricing guardrails, and runbook snippets for ops.

Scope (Q2):
- Finalize reservation windows and renewal SLA (30/60 day notice, soft lock period).
- Design flex-scale primitive: capacity tokens, burst-credit accounting, and policy surface for customers (max burst, cost cap).
- Implement control-plane APIs for reservations and dynamic hedging (backend work by ENG infra/runtime teams).
- Console UX: reservation calendar, forecast visualization, and toggle for flex-scale.
- Metrics & alerts: customer-visible cost delta, autoscale event success rate, and SLA breach alarms.

Out of scope for this ticket: billing system billing engine refactor (will be a dependency), on-prem air-gapped install flow (separate PM).
milestones: 2026-04-30: Console UX prototype and usability test
2026-05-15: Beta rollout to 3 customers and initial evaluation
okrs:
O1: Make Dedicated capacity predictable and cost-efficient for customers.
KR1: Reduce median underutilized reserved GPU hours by 20% across beta customers by end of Q2.

O2: Ensure autoscale reliability.
KR1: Achieve 99% successful flex-scale event rate without SLA degradation (p95 latency within target).

O3: Demonstrate cost hedging.
KR1: Limit overage costs from bursts to under 10% of committed spend during beta
acceptance_criteria: Approved RFC describing reservation cadence and lifecycle
Implemented flex-scale API with unit/integration tests and simulator results
Console UI for reservation and flex-scale controls tested with two PM/design reviews
Monitoring dashboards with baseline and alert thresholds configured
Beta trial with 3 customers and documented feedback loop
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Flex-scale leads to unexpected billing disputes. Mitigation: enforce cost caps, transparent forecasts, and pre-billing notifications.
Risk: Runtime contention during large bursts causing p95 regressions. Mitigation: conservative default burst limits, canary cohorts, and automatic fallback to hosted variants.
Risk: Sales/Legal objections to reservation lock windows. Mitigation: design a short soft-lock with opt-out and limited refund policy for early termination.
